newsitem.title: UK: Christies readying several big art auctions.
newsitem.headline: Christies readying several big art auctions.

text.p: British-based auctioneer and art specialist Christies International Plc said on Thursday it expected to start 1997 by selling a number of big single-owner collections after a lean year for large sales in 1996.

Commenting on its prospects in a statement accompanying its results for last year, which showed a significant 57 percent rise in pretax profits to 33.9 million pounds ($54 million), chairman Lord Hindlip called the outlook for first half sales "encouraging".

"Several important collections have already been consigned for sale, including a magnificent collection of Impressionist pictures from the John Langeloth Loeb and Frances Loeb collection, and Old Master, 19th century and Modern works from the collection of the late Lore and Rudolf Heinemann," Hindlip explained.
The profit jump in 1996 was achieved despite auction sales growth of only 9.0 percent to 1.016 billion pounds.
"The final result is especially pleasing because there were fewer single-owner collections available for sale in comparison with previous years," Hindlip added.
A noteable feature within the sales rise was a 31 percent increase from Asia/Pacific to a record $100 million, "principally as a result of very strong sales in Hong Kong".
Auction revenues grew faster than sales, up by 12.5 percent, helped by a new commission structure introduced in late 1995.

Auction costs, meanwhile, rose by about 6.4 percent, and the company said this was partly volume-driven and ought to be kept in check in future by more efficient catalogue production processes introduced after investments in recent years.

"Further benefits are expected to flow through to profitability in 1997," Christies added, noting that with the improved yield on all sales the operating profit from acutions had shot up by 69 percent.

In terms of strategy, the company said it was pressing on with plans to be ready to start up as one of the first foreign-owned auction houses in France once new legislation and regulations have been completed.

"In the light of the significance of the French art market, it is important that Christie's is in a position to react to the opportunities which we hope will soon be presented. It is our aim to hold sales in Paris in 1998 and we are finalising our strategy, which is likely to involve relocating our premises there," the company said.
A final dividend of 3.55 pence per share, up from 2.15 pence a year ago, is proposed to be paid to shareholders on May 23, giving a total for the year of 4.75 pence, up 70 percent.
In early trading after the results, Christies shares rose by 4 pence to 312-1/2 pence by 0915 GMT. ($ = 0.626 British Pounds)
